patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — OpenPhone and RingCentral share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

OpenPhone and RingCentral share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose OpenPhone only if your buying job matches “Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI —” rather than RingCentral's shape. Choose RingCentral only if your buying job matches “Enterprise-grade UCaaS / cloud phone platform (RingEX) with deep call routing, video, team” rather than OpenPhone's shape. Workflow advantage: OpenPhone leans shared coverage; RingCentral leans contact-center. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — OpenPhone and RingCentral share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: OpenPhone is Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI — Starter from $15/user/month annual.; RingCentral is Enterprise-grade UCaaS / cloud phone platform (RingEX) with deep call routing, video, team messaging and contact-centre options — Core from .
- Company-size focus: OpenPhone (solo, small-business, mid-market) vs RingCentral (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: OpenPhone-leaning — vs RingCentral-leaning contact-center.
- Researched limits: OpenPhone — US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story; RingCentral — Published seat floors are medium confidence — RingCentral often gates exact dollars behind quote/selector flows.

Limitations — OpenPhone: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story; Phone menus, automatic recording and deeper CRM require Business or above; RingCentral: Published seat floors are medium confidence — RingCentral often gates exact dollars behind quote/selector flows; Call recording and deeper CRM/CTI require Advanced or above.

Poor-fit cases: OpenPhone is a poor fit when that limitation bites: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story · RingCentral is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Published seat floors are medium confidence — RingCentral often gates exact dollars behind quote/selector flows · Avoid OpenPhone if you actually need RingCentral's motion (Enterprise-grade UCaaS / cloud phone platform (RingEX) with deep call routing, v)
